- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — keep forecast slightly above true for 1–2 periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); apply a “smooth decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after day 5.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days as baseline for adjustment.
- If true outcome is below 70, model often misses the drop; apply “floor correction” — if true < 70, forecast should not fall below 65–68 unless sentiment confirms strong bearish trend.
